evaluation_dimensions.name: Architecture
evaluation_dimensions.description: Technical stack, hardware accelerators (GPU/TPU/FPGAs), software stack (framework support, containerization, orchestration), and extensibility for custom AI models. Highlights differences in modularity, multi‑tenant isolation, and compliance‑ready design. [doc_001]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Enterprise Latency / Throughput
evaluation_dimensions.description: Measured end‑to‑end inference latency, training throughput (TFLOPs per dollar), network bandwidth, and scaling characteristics under enterprise workloads. Includes benchmark sources (MLPerf, internal PoCs) and variance across regions. [doc_002]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Pricing Predictability
evaluation_dimensions.description: Structure of usage‑based fees, reserved capacity discounts, tiered pricing, hidden costs (data egress, storage, support), and the availability of fixed‑price contracts or consumption caps. Emphasis on total cost of ownership (TCO) modeling for multi‑year procurement. [doc_003]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Advertised vs. Actual SLA
evaluation_dimensions.description: Comparison of vendor‑published service‑level agreements (availability, latency, support response) against third‑party monitoring data and customer‑reported incidents. Includes penalty clauses and remediation processes. [doc_004]

evaluation_dimensions.name: On‑Prem / Hybrid Readiness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Capabilities for edge, on‑premises, or hybrid deployments: hardware appliance options, software‑defined infrastructure, data residency controls, integration with existing enterprise clouds, and licensing models for mixed environments. [doc_005]

evaluation_dimensions.name: Customer Sentiment & Trust
evaluation_dimensions.description: Aggregated sentiment from analyst reports, Gartner/Forrester peer reviews, social‑media/ forum discussions, and Net Promoter Scores. Focus on trust factors such as security posture, roadmap transparency, and post‑sale support quality. [doc_006]

sources.purpose: Capture official architecture diagrams, pricing sheets, SLA contracts, and hybrid‑deployment guides.
Obtain independent latency/throughput results (e.g., MLPerf, SPEC AI) to validate performance claims.
Leverage Gartner, Forrester, and IDC assessments for market positioning and customer sentiment.
Collect qualitative insights on real‑world SLA adherence, support experience, and perceived value.
Use services like Downdetector, CloudHarmony, or custom synthetic tests to measure actual uptime and latency.
Identify pricing changes, new product announcements, and strategic shifts that affect procurement strategy.

actions: Create a master spreadsheet mapping each dimension to required data points.
Assign source owners (e.g., analyst team for benchmarks, legal for SLA contracts).
Download latest whitepapers, pricing calculators, and SLA PDFs from each competitor’s portal.
Request enterprise‑level architecture briefs via sales outreach.
Provision trial accounts on each platform.
Run standardized training and inference workloads (ResNet‑50, BERT) across multiple regions.
Record latency, throughput, and cost per run.
Cross‑reference vendor SLA language with public outage logs for the past 12 months.
Calculate actual availability percentages and compare to advertised figures.
Distribute a structured survey to existing enterprise customers (NPS, support rating, security confidence).
Scrape and code sentiment from relevant forums (Reddit r/MachineLearning, Stack Overflow tags).
Score each competitor on a 1‑5 scale per dimension.
Weight dimensions according to client procurement priorities (e.g., 30% pricing, 25% SLA).
Generate a heat‑map and a narrative briefing with leverage points for negotiation.

competitor_profiles.name: DataPulse Systems
competitor_profiles.positioning: Real‑time streaming data infrastructure and feature store for autonomous agents, aimed at financial institutions, fraud‑detection teams, and high‑frequency analytics workloads.

quotes.quote: CloudScale reduced our Groq and OpenAI token costs by 28% within the first month. However, documentation for custom Python middleware is sparse, and we experienced two 3-hour outages in Q2 where support disputed our 10x SLA credit claim citing upstream cloud network degradations.

The semantic cache hit rate hovers around 22% in production, which is lower than the advertised 40%. The UI dashboard is intuitive, but on-prem installation took four weeks instead of the promised 48 hours.

DataPulse is unrivaled for real-time latency. Our fleet routing agents query fresh sensor states in 6ms. Be careful with high-volume Kafka topics, however; overage fees doubled our invoice in month three before we configured filtering.
Reduced our MTTR from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod connection incidents. The safety guardrails are solid—it has never accidentally executed an unsafe command in production.

Veloce caught three sophisticated indirect prompt injection attempts during our clinical pilot. The false positive rate on medical abbreviations is slightly annoying (around 4%), but their customer support helped tune custom bypass dictionaries quickly.

outages_and_incidents.description: Two separate three‑hour service outages occurred in Q2; the customer’s request for a 10× SLA credit was denied by support, who attributed the failures to upstream cloud network degradations.

praise_and_positive_outcomes.description: Achieved a 28 % reduction in Groq and OpenAI token costs within the first month of deployment.
Mean time to recovery (MTTR) dropped from 45 minutes to 11 minutes for recurring database and pod‑connection incidents; safety guardrails prevented any unsafe command execution in production.
Detected three sophisticated indirect prompt‑injection attempts during a clinical pilot; support quickly tuned custom bypass dictionaries.
Delivered sub‑10 ms query latency (6 ms) for real‑time sensor data in a logistics routing use case.
The UI dashboard is described as intuitive, providing a positive user‑experience for monitoring.

usability_and_friction_points.description: Documentation for building custom Python middleware is described as sparse, creating integration friction.
Semantic cache hit rate observed at 22 %—significantly below the advertised 40 %—and on‑premise installation took four weeks versus the promised 48 hours.
High‑volume Kafka topics triggered unexpected overage fees, doubling the invoice in month three before proper filtering was applied.
False‑positive rate on medical abbreviations is around 4 %, which users find slightly annoying.
